full_judgment: 28. All parties including the OPW 1 and OPW 2 categorically admit that the pre-emptor was not present either at the time of signing the bainapatra or at the time of execution and registration the sale deed. It is also an admitted fact that the pre-emptor is owner of the suit property by inheritance and hence his ownership cannot be given away by the opposite parties No.2-4 through execution of a sale deed without his presence or consent. As the pre-emptor adduced evidence to prove that he learned of the sale on 22-2-2009 and filed the suit on 24-2-2009, the onus of burden of proof lies on the opposite parties to show that the pre-emptor at least had knowledge of the sale, but both OPW 1 and OPW 2 has given contradictory statements in their respective testimonies in this regard. OPW 2 has at one stage of his testimony additionally mentioned a "pre-sale discussion in Dhaka" which was not supported by the written statement of the opposite parties or by the statement of OPW 1. The sole evidence relied on by the Opposite Parties with regards to the pre-emptor's knowledge was the alleged counter-signature of the pre-emptor on the bainapatra, which too was discredited by the handwriting expert CW.1, who was not been cross examined, and hence it may be concluded that the opposite parties have failed to prove the pre-existing knowledge of pre-emptor from the date of execution of the bainapatra.
